Anil Kshetarpal, J.
1.

The petitioner here is the claimant in a petition filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor
Vehicles Act, 1988, to claim compensation for the injuries suffered by him in an accident.
2.  It is the case of the petitioner that when he was riding/driving the motorcycle bearing registration plate No. "HR-07-G-8878", he was involved in an accident.
In the FIR as well as the final report submitted by the police, the registration number of the motorcycle involved in the present case, is also mentioned as "HR-07-G-8878".

However, while filing the claim petition as well as filing an Mam Chand vs Niranjan Singh And Others on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57078314/
1 affidavit in his examination-in-chief, due to an inadvertent mistake, the registration plate number of the motorcycle has been wrongly mentioned as "HR-07-G-7788".

entities.text: Mam Chand vs Niranjan Singh And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An application filed by the petitioner to correct the aforesaid mistake, has been dismissed by the trial Court.
1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:145551 2023:PHHC:145551 3.

Heard the learned counsel representing the parties at length and with their able assistance,
perused the paper-book.
4. The petitioner herein is the registered owner of the vehicle i.e. HR-07-G-8878.
To err is a human.
It appears to be a bonafide inadvertent mistake of the petitioner while disclosing the registration plate number of his own vehicle.
The Court should have been indulgent in allowing such application particularly when in the FIR as well as the police report, the correct registration plate number has already been mentioned.
5. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, the present revision petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 09.04.2019 is set aside.
The petitioner is permitted to correct the mistake.
The Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is requested to proceed with the matter.
(Anil Kshetarpal) Judge November 16, 2023 "DK"
